title: The Art of Tea: Ceremony & Pastry Workshop
summary: Master the ancient ritual of Moroccan Mint Tea and learn to bake delicate 'Cornes de Gazelle' pastries with a local expert.
highlights: Learn the history and significance of Moroccan Mint Tea
Bake traditional pastries: Gazelle Horns or Briouates
Hosted in a private, serene Riad setting
Taste your creations with the host
Take home recipes and a small gift
description:
In Morocco, tea is not just a drink; it is a symbol of hospitality, friendship, and tradition. The phrase 'Atay Billah' (Tea by God) reflects its importance. In this hands-on workshop, you will go beyond the surface and learn the true art of the tea ceremony.

Hosted in a beautiful Riad, your instructor will explain the different types of mint (Spearmint, Absinthe, Pennyroyal) and how they change with the seasons. watch the ritual washing of the tea, the boiling, and the theatrical high pour—essential for aerating the tea and creating the 'Riza' (foam) crown.

While the tea steeps, you will get your hands floury making Moroccan pastries. Learn the delicate technique of rolling almond paste into 'Cornes de Gazelle' (Gazelle Horns) or folding honey-soaked Briouates. Sit down to enjoy your tea and warm pastries, discussing life in the Medina with your host.

title: Dinner with a Local Family: Authentic Home Dining
summary: Step inside a real Marrakech home for a shared meal, bridging the cultural gap and experiencing true Moroccan hospitality.
highlights: Exclusive invitation to a family home (not a restaurant)
Traditional home-cooked meal (recipes passed down generations)
Open conversation about culture, religion, and family life
description:
The best food in Morocco isn't found in 5-star restaurants; it's found in the home. However, as a traveler, it's hard to get invited inside. This experience opens that door.

You will be welcomed into the home of a local family in the Medina. This is not a cooking class (though you can help in the kitchen if you like); it is a dinner party. You will sit in the family salon, wash your hands with rose water, and learn to eat with your right hand using bread as a utensil—the traditional way.

The menu changes daily but expect hearty dishes like Rfissa (chicken with lentils and fenugreek), 7-Vegetable Couscous, or a family-style Tagine. The real value, however, is the conversation. Ask about their lives, traditions, and views. It is a moment of genuine human connection that transcends the tourist bubble.

title: Daily Bread: Traditional Baking Workshop
summary: Join the rhythm of the Medina by making your own bread, taking it to the communal oven (Farrane), and tasting it fresh.
highlights: Knead and shape 3 types of Moroccan bread (Khobz, Batbout, Msemmen)
Visit the community 'Farrane' to bake your loaf
Learn the cultural significance of bread in Islam
Enjoy a 'Goûter' (afternoon snack) with your fresh bread, honey, and cheese
Hands-on activity suitable for all ages
description:
In Morocco, bread is sacred. It is never thrown away; if fallen, it is kissed and placed aside. Every neighborhood has a detailed system centered around the 'Farrane' (communal oven), where families bring their dough twice a day.

In this workshop, you become part of that cycle. In a local kitchen, you'll learn to mix semolina and flour to create the perfect dough. You'll master the technique of shaping the round 'Khobz', layering the flaky 'Msemmen' (pancakes), and pan-frying 'Batbout' (Moroccan pita).

The highlight is the walk to the Farrane. You'll carry your tray of dough, hand it to the master baker, and watch him work his magic with the wood fire. The smell of your own bread baking is unforgettable. We finish by eating it hot, dipped in local olive oil, honey, and amlou (almond butter).

title: Fantasia Dinner Show - 1001 Nights
summary: Step into a folklore legend with this dinner show featuring horsemen charges, belly dancers, and traditional music under a caidal tent.
highlights: Dinner in a lavish Caidal Tent
Performances by Gnaoua, belly dancers, and acrobats
description:
Experience the pomp and pageantry of Moroccan history at the Chez Ali Fantasia complex. This is a large-scale dinner show that recreates the festive celebrations of the past. As you arrive, you are welcomed by tribesmen on horseback, musicians, and dancers lining the path to the tents.

You will dine in a traditional tent on a feast of Harira soup, roast lamb (Mechoui), Seven-vegetable Couscous, and dessert. Throughout the meal, different folklore groups from across Morocco pass by your table to perform.

The real show happens in the central arena. The 'Fantasia' or 'Tbourida' is a synchronized charge of Arab-Berber horsemen who fire their muskets into the air simultaneously—a display of power and coordination. It’s loud, colorful, and unlike anything else. The night ends with a belly dancing performance and a flying carpet illusion.

importantInfo: This is a large, tourist-oriented venue, not an intimate experience. It is great for families and groups wanting a party atmosphere.
The muskets are LOUD. Ear protection recommended for sensitive children.
In winter, the tents are heated but bringing a jacket is wise.

faqs.a: It is mass-catered but traditional and tasty. The lamb is the highlight.
It is definitely a 'show', but the horsemanship is genuine and impressive.

title: Golfing at the Foot of the Atlas
summary: Tee off on world-class greens with the snow-capped Atlas Mountains as your backdrop. A premium golfing experience including transfers and green fees.
highlights: 18 Holes at a top course (e.g., Royal Golf, Assoufid, Al Maaden)
Stunning scenery contrasting green fairways and red earth

description:
Marrakech is voted one of the world's best emerging golf destinations. The contrast of the emerald green sculpted fairways against the arid red earth and the white peaks of the Atlas Mountains is visually arresting. 

We organize your tee time at one of the city's prestigious courses. Choose from the historic Royal Golf (played by Churchill and Eisenhower), the modern sculpture-park style of Al Maaden, or the desert-style award-winning Assoufid. 

We handle the logistics: a private driver picks you up, takes you to the clubhouse, waits while you play your round, and brings you back. Whether you are a scratch golfer or a weekend warrior, playing here is a unique pleasure.

title: Wakeboarding at Waky Marrakech
summary: Cool off and catch some air at this world-class cable park set on an artificial lake with Atlas views.
highlights: Course suitable for beginners (kneeboard) and pros
Obstacles and jumps for advanced riders
description:
Surfing in the desert? Yes, it's possible. Waky Marrakech is a state-of-the-art cable park located in the Jardins de l'Atlas resort. A motorized cable pulls you around the purpose-built lake, eliminating the need for a boat and making it easy to learn or perfect your tricks.

Never tried it? Start with a kneeboard to get the feel of the water. Once confident, strap on the wakeboard. The consistent pull of the cable makes learning faster than behind a boat. For pros, the park features kickers, sliders, and rails to test your skills.

Even if you don't ride, the vibe is great. Relax by the infinity pool, order a burger and a cocktail, and watch the riders crash and fly. It’s the coolest place to be on a hot Marrakech day.

title: Horse Riding: Royal Equestrian Club & Forest
summary: Ride elegant Arabian-Barb horses through the eucalyptus forests or the Royal Club grounds.
highlights: Suitable for all levels (Walk, Trot, Gallop)
description:
Morocco has a deep equestrian tradition. Experience the grace of the Barb horse (the ancestor of the Thoroughbred) on a ride just outside the city walls. We partner with reputable stables that prioritize animal welfare.

Beginners will enjoy a gentle walk through the eucalyptus and olive groves, enjoying the birdsong and the scent of the forest. Experienced riders can pick up the pace, enjoying long canters along the sandy tracks. The horses are responsive and spirited yet safe. It’s a noble way to connect with nature.

summary: Start your trip stress-free with a private driver waiting for you at arrivals, helping with luggage, and driving you directly to your Riad/Hotel.
highlights: Meet & Greet inside the airport terminal
Flight tracking (we wait if you are delayed)

description:
Marrakech Menara Airport can be chaotic. Avoid the hassle of negotiating with taxi drivers or getting lost in the heat. Our private transfer service ensures a smooth start to your holiday.

Your driver will be waiting in the arrivals hall holding a clear sign with your name. They will assist with your bags and escort you to a clean, air-conditioned vehicle. During the drive, they can answer initial questions about the city. 

If you are staying in the Medina (car-free zone), the driver will take you to the nearest drop-off point and, if needed, call your Riad to send a porter (carossa) for your bags. No stress, no haggling, just service.

title: Stress-Free Airport Departure Transfer
summary: End your trip smoothly. We pick you up from your hotel and ensure you reach the airport with plenty of time for your flight.
description:
Don't leave your departure to chance. Book your ride back to Marrakech Menara Airport (RAK) in advance. We recommend a pickup time 3 hours before your flight departure (or 3.5 hours for busy periods).

Your driver will meet you at your hotel reception or the nearest accessible point for your Riad. Sit back and relax for the final ride through the Red City.

summary: Travel in comfort between Morocco's two major cities in a private vehicle with a professional driver.
highlights: Available for Airport (CMN) or City Centre
description:
Need to get to Casablanca? Skip the train schedule and the crowded taxis. Our private intercity transfer offers the flexibility to leave when you want.

The journey takes approximately 2.5 to 3 hours via the smooth highway. We use comfortable vehicles with plenty of legroom and trunk space. You can request a stop halfway for a coffee or restroom break. We can drop you off at a hotel in Casablanca city center or directly at Mohammed V International Airport (CMN) for your connecting flight.
